newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia to decide on Vereinsbank permit.
newsitem.headline: Latvia to decide on Vereinsbank permit.

text.p: The Latvian central bank will decide on Thursday whether to give a licence to Germany's Vereinsbank und Westbank, part of the Vereinsbank group, to open a branch in the Baltic state, the central bank said on Wednesday.
A central bank spokesman said the board would discuss the licence and make a decision at its regular meeting.
Vereinsbank is expected to be awarded the licence and become the second Western bank with a branch in Latvia after Societe Generale.
Estonian bank Hansapank earlier this year bought a Latvian bank in the first Baltic cross-border move.
Latvia during 1996 has gone through a recovery from a severe mid-1995 bank crisis caused by the closure of what was the largest bank, Banka Baltiya.

The central bank tightened controls to create a reliable and secure banking system for the former Soviet country, which portrays itself as the bridge between East and West and wants to attract foreign finance for the transit trade.
Banking officials say Scandinavian banks are also interested in setting up branches in Latvia. Finland's Merita already has a branch in Estonia.
